card.title: Stable log1mexp loss and analytic first derivative
card.text: For positive x, f(x)=log(1-exp(-x)). Mächler's documented stable method uses loss=log(-expm1(-x)) when x<=log(2), and loss=log1p(-exp(-x)) otherwise. log(2)=0.6931471805599453. The minus sign before expm1(-x) is essential: its result is negative. EIDOS analytic derivation: the positive first derivative can be written exp(-x)/(-expm1(-x)). This derivative identity is derived here, not attributed to the Rmpfr documentation. Preserve the input dtype; evaluate the selected loss branch lazily. Scope: the declared positive float32/float64 public normal-result domain, not subnormals, higher derivatives or training outcomes. This supplies a known repair, not a new discovery.

card.title: Preserve a small logarithmic increment with log1p
card.text: NumPy log1p(y) computes log(1+y) accurately for small real y even when forming 1+y would round to one. Its real finite domain requires y>-1. For large positive x, y=-exp(-x) is a small negative increment. Using log1p does not by itself verify the derivative, input dtype or validity at every branch boundary.
